Frequently Asked Questions

Planning & Zoning FAQ

9

  • The City Zoning Map is located on the webpage or under "Maps" on the Planning and Zoning Department. A staff member would be happy to help determine the zoning designation of your parcel. Please have the address or parcel number when calling.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • Each parcel within the City has setback requirements associated with the zoning designation. The required setbacks for front, rear, and side property lines are located in the Unified Development Code. Setbacks are measured from the property line. The best way to determine your property lines is to locate the actual property pins.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • The Unified Development Code contains a list of defined uses in each district within the City of Star. Each zoning designation has permitted, Uses Allowed with a Conditional Use Permit, and Non-allowed uses. Each district has its matrix and is located in the code.

    All uses that are not defined are considered automatically to be Conditional Uses and must go through the Public Hearing process.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • Development within certain flood zones requires a Flood Plain Development Permit and must meet the requirements of the City's Flood Hazard Ordinance.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • An original parcel of land may be divided one time, administratively, into not more than two (2) lots, parcels, or sites for transfer of ownership or development. This process does not require a public hearing, unless the City requires the applicant to plat the land division.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • Temporary living quarters are permitted in the City, in some cases, to house a member of the immediate family. The need for temporary living quarters for a family member must be justified for reasons of health, employment, or upkeep on the property. The structure may be permitted for two years and may not remain for more than six years. Other criteria may be required.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • If the business is allowed in a residential district, a home occupation application must be filled out and submitted to the City. In most cases, home occupations are allowed, but they shall meet certain criteria. Please see Section 8-5 3-27 Home Occupation for requirements.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • Please make an appointment with the planning department to have your property evaluated for flood zone location.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

  • The City Code contains the information necessary to build a fence. No sight-obscuring fencing shall be over three feet (3') tall within the vision triangle on corner lots. No fence shall be erected over three feet (3') in height in a front yard. No fence, on the perimeter boundary or within any required setback area, shall exceed a height of six feet (6') above adjacent grade.

    Planning & Zoning FAQ

Building FAQ

24

  • ZIP codes are created and managed by the United States Postal Service for mail delivery purposes and do not reflect municipal boundaries. In many areas, a single ZIP code may serve multiple cities or unincorporated areas.

    The Certificate of Occupancy issued by the City identifies the actual municipal jurisdiction responsible for permitting, inspections, and code compliance. For this reason, the address on the certificate may list the city where the property is physically located, even if the ZIP code is associated with a different “preferred city” in USPS records.

    This does not affect the validity of the Certificate of Occupancy or the deliverability of mail. The ZIP code ensures proper mail routing, while the city name reflects the correct governing jurisdiction.

    For property identification purposes, official records may also reference the parcel number and legal description maintained by the county.

    Building FAQ

    • All new construction
    • Structural additions and/or remodels
    • Sheds or outbuildings 200 sq. ft. or larger
    • Patio covers, pergolas, or awnings
      • Detached and larger than 200 sq. ft.
      • Attached (any size)
    • Re-roofing projects
    • Fences over 6 ft. tall
    • Retaining walls over 4 ft. from bottom of footing to top of wall
    • Setting manufactured homes
    • Replacement of siding (over 100 sq. ft.) on an existing house
    • Replacement of windows or doors where the openings are enlarged or reduced
    • Decks 30 or more inches above grade
    • Demolition


    Building FAQ

  • No building permit is required for a concrete slab of any size.

    Building FAQ

  • No building permit is required for IBC defined “Ag Buildings,” but they must comply with planning and zoning setbacks.

    Building FAQ

  • Architects, contractors, and homeowners can apply for permits. Architects can manage permits but cannot perform work. Contractors must have a current, valid license through the State of Idaho to apply for a permit.

    Building FAQ

  • If the homeowner pulls a permit, he/she must perform all work on the permit. Homeowners can pull permits on their primary or secondary residence without registering as a contractor with the state and must plan on living in the residence within 12 months of completion of the project. If the homeowner is not performing the work, a licensed contractor must pull the permit. 

    Homeowners are encouraged to speak with the building official prior to starting work. 


    Building FAQ

  • All permitting through the building department is completed online. You can find the permit portal here. You must be registered as a contractor or homeowner in our system prior to submitting a permit application online. Click here to see a how-to video.

    Building FAQ

  • Click on “Contractor Registration Form” on our website. The form will direct you to enter relevant contact and/or license information. If you have questions about this form, please contact the building department.

    Building FAQ

  • The access code you receive at time of registration is assigned specifically to the contractor or individual homeowner. This code is used to schedule inspections and upload files to existing permits. We do not share these codes with anyone whom it’s not assigned to. 

    Building FAQ

  • All payments are made online through our permit portal. This can be done with a credit card or e-check. Payment links are sent via email but can also be found by searching existing permits through our permit portal.

    Building FAQ

  • Currently, each permit must be paid for separately.

    Building FAQ

  • Inspections are scheduled by the contractor through our permit portal. We do not accept inspection requests on the phone or via email. Next-day inspections must be requested by 4:00 p.m. the business day before the inspection is needed. We do not schedule weekend inspections. Click here to see a how-to video.

    Building FAQ

  • If an inspection needs to be cancelled, please email the building department at building@staridaho.org . Permit number, address, and type of inspection should be referenced. 

    Building FAQ

  • If changes need to be made to a scheduled inspection, please email the main building department as soon as possible. Please reference the permit number, address, and what needs to be changed on the inspection. We are not always able to accommodate changes and re-inspection fees could apply.

    Building FAQ

  • We do not schedule rough and final inspections for the same day. If you need more details about this, please contact your inspector directly.

    Building FAQ

  • Ada County Assessor’s website shows city boundaries. Please enter the address in question on this website and use the interactive map:

    https://apps.adacounty.id.gov/PropertyLookup/SearchProperty . 

    If you still have questions or your address does not populate with permit applications, please contact the building department.

    Building FAQ

  • At any time, you can check the status of your permit and/or inspection. To do this, please visit https://staridpermit.portal.iworq.net/portalhome/staridpermit.

    1. Select “Permit Portal.”
    2. Select “Search Existing Permits” on the upper left-hand side of the screen
    3. Search by permit number or address.
    4. Click on the actual permit number to view all details related to your permit. This information is updated in real time. 

    Click here to see an instructional how-to video.

    Building FAQ

  • Some inspectors will leave notes on site, while others will leave notes in the portal. If you would like to speak to an inspector and do not currently have their contact information, please contact the building department.

    Building FAQ

  • The length of review time depends on the type of permit and if our department has all necessary information to process your permit. Assuming our department has all the necessary information and paperwork, no revisions are made, and no corrections are needed, typical review times are as follows:

    • Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing: same day if the associated building permit is approved.
    • Demolition, Re-roofing, Siding: same day
    • Small residential projects: 2-4 weeks
    • Larger residential projects: Approximately 4-6 weeks
    • Commercial projects: 4-6 weeks

    *These review times can fluctuate due to volume, holidays, and extenuating circumstances. Review times will be extended by 3-4 weeks per revision or correction that is made or required.

    Building FAQ

  • Please call or email the building department as soon as you know you need an extension. If you wait until after the permit is expired, there could be additional fees to re-instate the permit.

    Building FAQ

  • Copies of building plans can be found on the portal if the permit was submitted after January 2024. If you need copies of plans prior to January 2024, you will need to submit a Public Records Request through the City Clerk's Office. Please note that the building department is only required to keep residential permitting records for 2 years. 

    Building FAQ

  • We do not expedite plans for a fee.

    Building FAQ

  • Although you should always contact both, it is best to start with your HOA. The building department has no authority over HOAs, and your HOA may have stricter guidelines on the types of projects that are allowed on your property.

    Building FAQ

  • Please contact Planning and Zoning at pandz@staridaho.org 

    Building FAQ

Vendor FAQs and Examples

8

  • Requires Temporary Use Permit and Temporary Vendor Permit (Star Unified Development Code §8-1B-4).

    Vendor FAQs and Examples

  • The truck must have the property owner’s permission. The City recommends following best practices for safety and neighborhood consideration (Star City Code §2-4-2).

    Vendor FAQs and Examples

  • Yes, but it requires property owner permission and a Temporary Vendor Permit (Star City Code §2-4-2).

    Vendor FAQs and Examples

  • Yes. Ice cream trucks (or any mobile sales vehicle) require a Door-to-Door Sales Permit (Star City Code §2-4-2).

    Vendor FAQs and Examples

  • The event host must complete a Special Event Permit and apply for Temporary Vendor Permits for all participating vendors (Star City Code §6-1-3).

    Vendor FAQs and Examples

  • You will need a Temporary Vendor Permit (Star City Code §2-4-2).

    Vendor FAQs and Examples

  • No. Vending is not allowed in City parks (Star City Code §6-1-3).

    Vendor FAQs and Examples

  • Children age 14 and under do not need a vendor permit if they are selling on:

    • Their own property, or

    • Private property with the property owner’s permission.

    They cannot sell on City property, including all City parks (Star City Code §6-1-3).
